def is_plain_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a single plain file name: non-empty, not "." or "..",
    and with no path separator, drive colon or NUL character."""
    ex is_plain_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_plain_name("") == False
    ex is_plain_name("..") == False
    ex is_plain_name("../secret") == False
    ex is_plain_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_plain_name("sub\\x.txt") == False
    if name.char_count() == 0:
        return False
    if name == "." or name == "..":
        return False
    for c in name.chars():
        if c == "/" or c == "\\" or c == ":" or c == "\0":
            return False
    return True

def first_readable(names: list[str]) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the first name in names that can be read as a file inside the
    directory `notes` (relative to the working directory), or "" when none can.
    Names are untrusted: fs is confined with `with fs = fs.sub("notes")`, and
    names that are not plain file names are skipped, so nothing outside `notes`
    is ever read. Missing or unreadable files are skipped."""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        for name in names:
            if not is_plain_name(name):
                continue
            text: str | None = fs.read_text(name) else None
            if text is not None:
                return text
    return ""
